gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Noto Sans Lepcha reads friendly, with lowercase as sturdy as cast iron capitals. Quilon sits above it with a commanding editorial voice and gentle swings in stroke weight, while the sans below stays nearly uniform and lets the headline do the talking.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Noto Sans Limbu brings tall-bodied small letters and curves that gape wide open, a contemporary and approachable texture. And Quilon's thin strokes beside moderately weighty stems give the heading an editorial edge that the plain sans simply never tries to match.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-lydian: Approachable, with capitals barely taller than the lowercase beside them. Quilon brings an editorial, commanding heading with moderate stroke contrast, and Noto Sans Lydian is the low-contrast sans-serif that gives it room, which is the pairing's real strength.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-mahajani: Noto Sans Mahajani is modern and professional, its lowercase standing tall against the capitals and its e opening like a funnel. Over a long page, Noto Sans Mahajani would feel smooth and unhurried, while Quilon's moderate stem-to-hairline ratio stays up in the heading.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-malayalam: Commanding headlines, friendly text underneath. Quilon earns its keep big and short, where its modest gap between stems and hairlines shows, while Noto Sans Malayalam fills the lines with a dense middle zone and an s with generous openings.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-mandaic: Noto Sans Mandaic has lowercase rising close to the capitals and curvy letters that feel unclamped, set against Quilon's quiet stroke modulation up top. A long read would flow without friction.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-mayan-numeral: Quilon leads with editorial authority and soft accents of heavier strokes. Noto Sans Mayan Numerals follows with tall-bodied small letters and a visibly gaping c, a low-contrast sans-serif that lets the heading's rhythm stay in front.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-medefaidrin: Tall, crisp lowercase meets a heading whose stems run a little heavier than its hairlines, with no ink pooling where curves turn in. Quilon commands, Noto Sans Medefaidrin stays out of the way.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-meetei-mayek: Quilon carries an editorial swagger, with a subtle gradient of weight along each curve that rewards a closer look. Noto Sans Meetei Mayek does the opposite job, offering a modern sans with large lowercase eyes and rounds that gap like a cracked bangle.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-mende-kikakui: Quilon's moderate thick-thin ratio and large open counters give the heading its commanding editorial presence. But Noto Sans Mende Kikakui, a clean sans-serif with daylight through every curve and tall lowercase, keeps the text modern and low-key beneath it.
